walkthroughs.body_html:
Sociological Theories, Methods & Research — a core area of GCSE Sociology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Sociological Theories, Methods & Research brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Sociological Theories, Methods & Research.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

Verstehen
Praxis
Alienation

mcqs.q: Which research method involves in-depth participant observation?
options: Survey
Experiment
Ethnography
Content analysis

mcqs.q: What is Merton's strain theory of crime?
options: Snowball sampling is only used in winter research.
Strain theory says criminals have psychological strain disorders.
Strain theory says people commit crime because they are stressed.

Crime results from a mismatch between cultural goals (success, wealth) and legitimate means of achieving them — those who can't access legitimate means may innovate (crime), ritualise, retreat or rebel.

mcqs.q: What is the postmodern view of identity?
options: Identity is fixed by class, gender, and ethnicity at birth.
Everyone has the same identity in postmodern society.
Identities are fluid, fragmented, and constructed through consumption and choice.
Snowball sampling is only used in winter research.
Snowball sampling is a type of random sampling.
Snowball sampling is only used in winter research.
Everyone has the same identity in postmodern society.

When studying hard-to-reach or hidden populations (drug users, undocumented migrants) where a sampling frame doesn't exist — participants recruit further participants. It sacrifices representativeness for access.
